intended_object: For an arrow e : i → j of a quiver Q, the canonical morphism of representations P_j → P_i between indecomposable projectives that puts e in front of each path out of j. Under Hom(P_j, M) ≅ M_j it is the element e of (P_i)_j, i.e. right multiplication by e between the left ideals kQ·e_j → kQ·e_i. This comes from the docstring and the module doc, which uses it for the standard resolution 0 → ⊕ P_j → P_i → S_i → 0.
explanation:
The definition applies the library's universal-property morphism `indecProjRepHom j (P_i) x` to x = the basis vector of the path `e.toPath` in (P_i)_j.

`indecProjRepHom` sends the basis vector of a path q : j → b to `M.map q x`. In P_i, a path acts by concatenation on the right (`indecProjRep_map_basis`). So the basis vector of q goes to the basis vector of `e.toPath.comp q`, which is the path e followed by q. The lemma `indecProjRepArrowHom_app_basis` proves exactly this. This is the textbook map P(e): P_j → P_i used in the projective resolution of the simple S_i (Assem–Simson–Skowroński, Ch. III). The direction and the composition order are both correct.

The `[Field k]` assumption is inherited from the library-wide `QuiverRep k Q` setting. This definition adds no restriction of its own, and the Q, i, j and universes are fully general. Mathlib has no quiver-representation projectives, so there is no counterpart.
